summary: The run developed a functional damage-heavy Ironclad deck and reached Act 2, but repeated fights steadily reduced HP until only 19 HP remained before the final combat. The clearest visible failure was the final combat's first turn, where the agent spent energy attacking and then ended with three Defends still available, leaving no block before the enemies' next attack cycle.

lessons.title: At critical HP, convert unused energy into immediate block
lessons.situation: When entering a turn at very low HP with no block and defensive cards legally playable, especially before enemies can attack.
lessons.lesson: Prioritize surviving the current enemy cycle over marginal damage: play available Defends or other mitigation before ending the turn, unless lethal damage is clearly guaranteed.
evidence_points: The final combat began at 19/80 HP and 0 Block; after playing Bash+ and Headbutt, the agent ended Turn 1 with three Defends still in hand and all three were legal alternatives.
On Turn 2, both enemies had attack-related intents while the player was still at 19 HP, requiring Impervious to avoid immediate danger.
lessons.reasoning: The first turn established a dangerous zero-block state despite legal defensive actions, and the next turn confirms that enemy attacks were an immediate concern. At 19 HP, preserving health was more important than spending the whole opening turn on damage setup.

lessons.title: Stop adding redundant attacks when attrition is already severe
lessons.situation: After several combats have caused substantial HP loss and the deck already contains many attack cards, particularly when a reward offers defensive or utility alternatives.
lessons.lesson: Favor mitigation, draw, exhaust synergy, or other survivability tools over another ordinary attack when the deck's damage is already adequate; make the deck better at preventing the HP loss that limits future fights.
evidence_points: The final 23-card deck contains three Strikes, Bash+, two Headbutts, Reckless Charge, Pummel, two Sword Boomerangs, Hemokinesis, Thunderclap, and other damage cards, alongside only four Defends and a limited set of defensive tools.
The run's HP repeatedly declined during Act 1 and Act 2: it was 52/80 after the early Act 1 fights, 20/80 after the Hexaghost fight, and 19/80 before the final Act 2 combat.
At Act 1 Floor 11, the reward alternatives included Sentinel, but Sword Boomerang was chosen; at Act 1 Floor 2, Sentinel and Dark Embrace were also alternatives to the chosen Pummel.
lessons.reasoning: The exact alternatives were not always strictly better, but the repeated attack additions and large HP losses indicate that future rewards should be evaluated for survivability rather than continuing to increase damage density. The deck did eventually acquire Impervious, Feel No Pain+, and Disarm, but the low HP shows that defensive development came too slowly or too inconsistently.
